source_text.body_text:
So he ran. He gave up the throne, slept in the dirt, and starved himself for years, sure that suffering would hand him the meaning he craved.

It handed him nothing. Sitting under a tree, he finally saw what he had missed all along: rich or poor, indulgent or starving, everyone suffers.

He would become the Buddha, and this was his very first teaching.
other_story_text: If pain is unavoidable, Manson argues, the question is which pain is worth carrying.

source_text.body_text:
If pain is unavoidable, Manson argues, the question is which pain is worth carrying.

For half his life, Manson dreamed of being a rock star: the crowds, the noise, the fame. But he never practiced. He loved the daydream of success, not the daily grind of guitar practice.

source_text.body_text:
Real fulfillment doesn't come from eliminating problems, but from choosing the specific set of problems you are willing to solve every day.

Before chasing any goal, stop asking how badly you want the reward. Ask instead whether you can stand the daily grind it demands; commit to it only, if the answer is yes.
